claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a red gas cylinder with a silver valve assembly in a car trunk.
Capacity is not shown in Photo 0; the collar stamping is not visible.
No import markings or origin are visible; wear is present but provenance is unconfirmed.

risks.risk: The cylinder may be empty or only partially filled.
risks.proof: A video of gas flowing through a regulator attached to the valve, or a photo of the cylinder on a scale showing full weight.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an empty cylinder shell only.

risks.proof: A close-up photo of the collar stamping showing the water capacity or weight marking.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unmarked cylinder of unknown capacity.

risks.risk: The certification or expiry date may be missing or expired.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the collar stamping showing the test or expiry date.
risks.if_unproven: priced as uncertified or expired and not legally refillable.

risks.risk: The valve or body may leak or have hidden damage.
risks.proof: A clip of a soapy-water leak test on the valve and seams, or a pressure test.
risks.if_unproven: priced as leaking or damaged and unsafe to use.

risks.risk: No regulator or hose is included.
risks.proof: A photo showing a regulator and hose together with the cylinder.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cylinder only, without accessories.

proof_requests: Close-up of the cylinder collar showing capacity and expiry date.
Video of gas flowing through a regulator attached to the valve.
Photo showing any regulator and hose included with the cylinder.
Clip of a soapy-water leak test on the valve and seams.
response.reason: The witness identifies a red gas cylinder with visible scuffs; even without proof of capacity, contents, certification, or accessories, it can be valued at its worst case as an empty, uncertified cylinder without accessories.
